chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Husayn ibn Usman, from Ibn Muskan, from Aban ibn Taghlib, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the one who is killed in the Way of Allah, should he be washed, enshrouded, and embalmed? He (peace be upon him) said: 'He is buried as he is in his clothes, except if there is still breath in him and then he dies, for then he is washed, enshrouded, embalmed, and prayer is performed upon him. Indeed, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) performed prayer upon Hamza and enshrouded him because he had been stripped.'
ai.seo_question: What is the difference in funeral rites between a martyr who dies instantly and one who survives their wound?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi delineates the juristic distinction between a 'true' martyr who dies instantly and one who survives the wound, a nuance rooted in the precedent of Hamza ibn Abd al-Muttalib, whose body was washed and prayed over because he had been stripped of his armor. This ruling highlights the Shia emphasis on the physical state of the deceased at the moment of death as the determinant for funeral rites, linking the legal status of martyrdom to both spiritual reward and practical ritual treatment.
